checked_classes: Build-versus-adopt blind spots — The artifact compares existing UAR primitives with a timing library, a durable job library, and a workflow platform. It assigns UAR-specific authority and transaction semantics to UAR while requiring an exact-version scheduler fit gate before adoption.

Unevaluated candidates — All seven candidates have verdicts, supporting evidence, risks, and decision rationales. Conditional adoption and reference-only dispositions are explicitly distinguished from permission to install dependencies.

Maintenance and unverifiable landscape claims — External candidates include release/version checks and primary-source references. The artifact identifies mutable main-branch documentation, stale indexed Temporal descriptions, unresolved licensing, and the absence of compatibility tests rather than treating them as settled adoption evidence.

Missing solution categories — The candidate set covers timing, persistent job dispatch, workflow orchestration, existing memory infrastructure, transactional persistence, and provider framing. No required capability in the supplied goals demonstrates a missing solution category that would invalidate the recommendations.

Contradictions with assessment or goals — The artifact explicitly updates the assessment's publication uncertainty, traces effective dependency inputs without approving policy-pin divergence, and preserves the unreproduced status of runtime findings. Both local operation and shared hosting remain mandatory first-release gates.

Project constraints and unsupported support claims — No separate constraints were supplied. Backend and entry-point mappings are labeled proposals, unresolved mappings block support claims, and Postgres and direct embedded SDK parity are not silently asserted.
